reuse.why: Holidays are routed through the existing getDateWithWeekendRule at every caller and a shared isHoliday is added, but the daily-skip rule and the weekend-or-holiday test are re-written at each site instead of being one helper.

duplication.why: The 'is this day unavailable' check (isWeekend || isHoliday) appears three times (inside getDateWithWeekendRule, getNextDate's daily loop, getDatesInRange's filter), the daily-skip rule exists twice in different shapes, and getDatesInRange repeats getUpcomingDates' RSchedule/try/captureBreadcrumb scaffolding.

placement.why: Date rules sit in shared/schedules.ts as in the tree, but the daily-skip logic for ranges lives in the server handler rather than next to the shared rule, so other callers (getUpcomingDates, schedule-template) do not get it.

scope.why: Focused on the requested schedule-date features; minor noise such as a second date-fns import for parseISO.

maintainability.why: Daily skipping is decided separately in getNextDate (bounded 366-step loop) and getDatesInRange (filter), and not at all in the upcoming-dates and template paths, so the rule will drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange and shared/schedules.ts getNextDate each implement the daily weekend/holiday skip with their own isWeekend||isHoliday checks instead of one shared date-adjustment function

disguised_duplication.where: The daily-skip rule appears as a loop over occurrences in getNextDate and as a .filter predicate in getDatesInRange; the unavailable-day predicate is an inline lambda in getDateWithWeekendRule and inline conditions elsewhere

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithWeekendRule gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate adds a daily-only special branch before calling it; getDatesInRange re-implements the daily skip around it
